name: math.big
doc:
math.big: arbitrary-precision Int, Rat and Decimal.

Values are immutable: every operation returns a new value (unlike Go's
z.Add(x, y)), so copies may share storage safely. The method names are
those of the operator interfaces (Add, Sub, Mul, Div, Rem, Neg,
Compare, Equals), so `+ - * / %`, unary `-`, `== !=` and `< <= > >=`
work on Int, Rat and Decimal (DESIGN.md "Перегрузка операторов"). Magnitudes are []uint32 limbs; the limb arithmetic (Karatsuba
multiplication, Knuth division, base conversion) is C
(runtime/src/std_math_big.c).

items.name: ParseDecimal
items.doc:
Parses "-12.340", "+5", ".5", "1e-3", "2.5E2"; the scale is the number
of digits after the point minus the exponent (at least 0).
items.summary: Parses "-12.340", "+5", ".5", "1e-3", "2.5E2"; the scale is the number of digits after the point minus the exponent (at least 0).

0x, 0o, 0b selects the base (default 10). Underscores between digits
are allowed with base 0.
items.summary: Parses an integer with optional sign in base 2..36, or base 0: prefix 0x, 0o, 0b selects the base (default 10).

items.name: Decimal
items.doc:
A fixed-point decimal: unscaled * 10^-scale (scale >= 0), exact for
Add, Sub and Mul; Div rounds to a chosen scale. The zero value is 0.
String keeps the scale ("1.50" stays "1.50").
items.summary: A fixed-point decimal: unscaled * 10^-scale (scale >= 0), exact for Add, Sub and Mul; Div rounds to a chosen scale.

items.name: Int
items.doc: An arbitrary-precision integer. The zero value is 0.

members.name: Quo
members.doc:
Truncated division (rounds toward zero, like Go's Quo and Zell's
int /). Panics on division by zero.
members.summary: Truncated division (rounds toward zero, like Go's Quo and Zell's int /).

members.name: Rem
members.doc: Remainder of Quo: has the sign of this (like Go's Rem and %).
members.summary: Remainder of Quo: has the sign of this (like Go's Rem and %).

members.name: Div
members.doc:
Truncated division, the operator `/`: same as Quo, so that `/` and
`%` (Rem) behave like Zell's int operators (a == a/b*b + a%b).
Go's Euclidean Div is DivEuclid here.
members.summary: Truncated division, the operator `/`: same as Quo, so that `/` and `%` (Rem) behave like Zell's int operators (a == a/b*b + a%b).

members.name: DivEuclid
members.doc: Euclidean division (Go's Div): the remainder Mod(y) is always >= 0.
members.summary: Euclidean division (Go's Div): the remainder Mod(y) is always >= 0.

members.name: Compare

members.summary: The same as Cmp (the Ordered operator-interface name).

members.summary: this >> n (n >= 0), rounding toward negative infinity like Go.

members.name: Exp
members.signature: func Exp(y Int, m Int) Int!
members.doc:
this^y mod m (m zero: no modulus; y < 0 with a modulus: the inverse
power, error if none). Panics for y < 0 without a modulus.
members.summary: this^y mod m (m zero: no modulus; y < 0 with a modulus: the inverse power, error if none).

members.name: ModInverse
members.doc: The inverse of this modulo m: x with this*x ≡ 1 (mod m), 0 <= x < |m|.
members.summary: The inverse of this modulo m: x with this*x ≡ 1 (mod m), 0 <= x < |m|.

members.name: GCD
members.doc: The greatest common divisor of |this| and |y| (Euclid).
members.summary: The greatest common divisor of |this| and |y| (Euclid).

members.name: ProbablyPrime
members.doc:
Miller-Rabin with n pseudo-random bases plus the first 12 prime
bases (deterministic below 3.3e24). Never wrong for primes; the
chance a composite passes is at most 4^-(n+12).
members.summary: Miller-Rabin with n pseudo-random bases plus the first 12 prime bases (deterministic below 3.3e24).
